ga_allenbrook.blurb: Allenbrook is a small, steep, blocky cliff in the Roswell stretch of the Chattahoochee corridor north of Atlanta, hidden behind a historic house and above a creek. Nineteen climbs are listed: eight boulder problems from V2 to V4, eight top-rope lines, two trad routes and a single sport route, with roped grades running from the 5.6 range up through 5.12. The face is overhanging, so expect sustained, pumpy climbing with few rests rather than a mellow beginner wall. Almost everything is done on top rope off tree anchors. Tree cover keeps it shaded for most of the day, which suits summer but means it can stay damp after rain.

ga_project_boulder.blurb: Project Boulder is a single block with nineteen problems, and it is the first boulder you meet on the short walk in from the trailhead at the base of Mount Yonah in northeast Georgia. The problems cover nearly the whole range, from V0 and V1 warm-ups through a mid-grade middle to a cluster of V6 to V9 lines and one problem near V11. One side of the block has gentler, kid-friendly problems. The landing is flat but not always solid, so bring more than one pad, and keep the creek below the problems free of stacked sticks.
ga_project_boulder.approach: Short walk on the trail from the parking area; this is the first boulder you reach, on the right.

ga_kashmir_area.blurb: Kashmir Area is a bouldering sector at Boat Rock, the small urban boulder field on the west side of Atlanta. Eighteen problems are listed, mostly easy to mid-range: a good number of VB to V2 lines, a handful around V3 and V4, and only a few harder problems above that. The main block can be climbed on every side, with bulging faces, cracks and crystal-studded holds, and the leftward finger crack that gives the sector its name is visible from the parking lot, which makes the boulder easy to find. It is a good stop for a varied, short session.

ga_mangler_area.blurb: Mangler Area is a short line of small cliffs and boulders on the bank of the Chattahoochee River, one of the sectors of the Palisades northwest of downtown Atlanta. It holds eighteen climbs, all bouldering apart from a single roped line. Grades are friendly at the bottom end, with plenty from V0 to V4 and a handful of harder problems, topping out with a V10. Problems are around ten feet tall and need a pad.

ga_gumby_slab_hanging_garden.blurb: This cliff on Mount Yonah, the granite dome in the north Georgia mountains, sits between the Lowers and the Main Face. Seventeen routes are listed, twelve trad and five sport, graded from 5.5 to 5.9 with most in the 5.6 to 5.8 range. The lines are moderate and well protected, so a rack is worth carrying, though the tops of some easy routes can feel run out. The lower Hanging Garden part sits under the water runoff from the face above and stays wet for days after rain, although routes dry faster than you would think, especially in the afternoon. The approach is a steep scramble up from the Lowers.

ga_helicopter_area.blurb: Helicopter Area is a compact sector of the Rocktown boulder field on Pigeon Mountain in northwest Georgia. It is pure bouldering on a short, angled wall of sandstone that is usually shady, with sixteen problems. Grades start at V3 and run up to V9, with the bulk in the V4 to V5 range and a few harder problems above that, so it suits climbers who have already outgrown the easy end. It is reached by a trail that drops down past a well-known roof and through a wide corridor. A couple of pads and a spotter are advised, and some tops are lichen-covered.

ga_vagina_area.blurb: This is a cluster of boulders in the Rocktown field on Pigeon Mountain in northwest Georgia, down the trail from a landmark boulder called the Orb. Of its sixteen climbs fifteen are boulder problems, with one trad line, and the grades spread widely: a few V2 to V3 problems, a solid middle of V4 to V6, and several hard ones between V8 and V10. The boulders are easy to spot, and the front corridor is known for some of the best and stiffest problems. Rocktown rock is sandstone with slopers, crimps, huecos and rails.
